subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should OpenClaw add native backup exclude-pattern controls now, and which defaults and protected paths should become part of the core CLI contract?
rationale: The missing capability is clear, but the final behavior chooses a security and restore-completeness boundary for native backups rather than a purely mechanical fix.

options.title: Review linked PR as canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 to settle defaults, protected paths, manifest/JSON compatibility, proof, and conflict resolution before landing or narrowing it.

options.title: Narrow to custom excludes first
options.body: Accept only explicit `--exclude` and `--exclude-file` controls while deferring smart defaults until restore completeness and security expectations are clearer.

options.title: Defer native excludes
options.body: Keep core backups coarse, document the current scope, and direct optional backup strategies such as Keep My Claw to ClawHub after an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Review linked PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 to settle defaults, protected paths, manifest/JSON compatibility, proof, and conflict resolution before landing or narrowing it.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest combined history signal across the original backup CLI review/co-author context and the current backup helper refactor.
